# Browser GIF evidence

Produce one truthful GIF from one isolated run of the changed build. This skill owns capture, encoding, verification and optional publication. Whether the UI is acceptable is a separate judgment.

## Defaults

Apply this skill's use-site default only when neither the request nor existing project instructions choose one. Treat existing instructions as authoritative read-only input; do not ask for, create, modify, or copy instructions merely to select a default.

## Evidence default

When a change alters user-visible browser UI behavior, generate and verify GIF evidence by default. When the task also creates or updates a pull request, attach the verified GIF there. Without a pull-request task, keep the evidence local.

The project's explicit instructions may select equivalent evidence or waive the default for a named change. A fixture recording is allowed only when the user explicitly requests it or the project's evidence policy selects that form. Do not use a mock transport, synthetic interaction, or test-only hook unless the user or project policy explicitly requires that substitute.

Do not claim completion when the build, browser, real scenario, media tools or publication facility needed by the requested evidence is unavailable. Preserve completed work and hand off the missing capability, unfinished evidence and next step.

## Establish evidence scope

- Identify the exact commit and tree that will be demonstrated. Require a clean worktree before building; only ignored evidence paths may appear after capture starts. Stop when tracked or untracked source changes would contribute to the demonstrated build.
- Record the application origin, transport and any mode override or browser-state exception.
- Read the project's build, start, browser-control, evidence-directory and publication instructions. Missing instructions permit a working default, not an invented project mechanism.
- Use one isolated application run: fresh application state, workspace, session data and browser storage. Existing user browser state is an explicit exception, not an invisible default.
- Keep every frame and artifact from one run. If capture fails, discard the run and start again; never splice a newer outcome into an older capture.
- Use one demonstrated page and a short story of three to six meaningful states. Wait on semantic page state rather than fixed sleeps; a fixed wait may hold a verified frame for reading, but cannot establish readiness.
- Preserve animations and scrolling that carry the demonstrated state, and review the complete selected interval including intermediate states.
- When demonstrating a tool call, rejection or recovery, expose the tool identity, status or stable error code, downstream result and any transient running state that carries the behavior.
- State whether the run used the real product path and real external services, a fixture, a mock or another substitute. Never read or expose credential values, personal data, unrelated tabs or notifications.

## Capture

Use the project's browser-control capability first. When continuous video is available, record video in the same browser context that exercises the application. When only screenshots are available or the user requests a storyboard, capture verified states from one isolated run in a stable filename order.

When browser control is unavailable and the project declares an isolated Playwright fallback, use that declaration rather than installing another driver. Match `viewport` and recorded-video dimensions explicitly so text is not scaled down silently. Retain the page video handle before closing the context and await the context close before saving or encoding the video.

Store raw video, screenshots, capture notes and QA frames in a project-declared ignored path. When the project declares none, use a fresh temporary directory outside the tracked tree and report its path. Do not commit evidence media to a branch.

Close browser contexts, stop servers started for the run and remove transient browser profiles on both success and failure. Stop a server by its recorded PID or an exact command-line match; a broad `pkill -f` pattern can match and kill the shell that launched it. Keep the captured evidence and report the first incomplete cleanup step.

## Encode

The bundled Node encoder requires `ffmpeg` and `ffprobe`. It refuses to install missing media tools.

```sh
export SKILL_DIR=/absolute/path/to/this/skill
node "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/encode-browser-gif.mjs" \
  /absolute/path/to/demo.webm \
  /absolute/path/to/demo.gif \
  --start 2 --end 32 --speed 2 --final-hold 3
```

Video flags select one continuous interval. Choose `--start` and `--end` from observed source-video times, not guessed wall-clock offsets. For a screenshot directory, use `--pattern` to match filenames with `*` or `?`, then use `--durations`:

```sh
node "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/encode-browser-gif.mjs" \
  /absolute/path/to/frames \
  /absolute/path/to/demo.gif \
  --pattern '*.png' \
  --durations 1.5,1.5,1.5,3.5
```

Read the JSON summary. Shrink `--max-width` first, then `--colors` or `--fps`, when the artifact exceeds the default 5 MiB limit. Disclose any trimming, speed change or final hold beside the published evidence. Resolve the output path before overwriting; pass `--force` only when replacing that existing evidence is intentional. An existing output is replaced only after a complete GIF has encoded and passed validation. An encoding or validation failure leaves the previous output unchanged.

## Verify

1. Confirm the encoded path, interval or screenshot count, speed, frame count, dimensions, duration and byte size from the encoder summary.
2. Inspect the encoded GIF itself. If the viewer shows only its first frame, decode representative frames with `ffmpeg`.
3. Confirm that the sequence shows the intended cause and outcome, remains legible and contains no sensitive data.
4. Run `git status --short` and confirm raw media and the GIF lie only under ignored or untracked evidence paths.
5. State whether the evidence is real, fixture-based or otherwise substituted.

## Publish

Publication occurs only when the task includes creating or updating a pull request. Read [the publication contract](references/publication.md) before attaching evidence.

The contract owns the live-head check and attachment procedure. Publish only evidence that still corresponds to the demonstrated pull request's current head; re-record when it does not.

## Completion

Evidence is complete when one verified GIF, or the ordered set of verified GIF parts from one run, exists; its run and source are identified; its content is legible and safe; and every publication step requested by the task has succeeded. Otherwise report the exact missing capability or artifact and the resumable next step.

# Publishing GIF evidence

Use this contract only when the task includes publishing evidence to a change request. Capture and encoding remain local until this step.

## Require a publication mechanism

Read the project's declaration for its review platform and attachment mechanism. The project owns the command, authentication requirements, supported hosting service and body format.

For a GitHub pull request, `gh --attach` is the working example. Run `gh --version` before relying on it. Attachment requires `gh` 2.99.0 or later, a repository on `github.com` and write access; GitHub Enterprise Server is not supported. When the installed client does not support attachment, keep the verified local GIF and report the requirement without installing or upgrading the client.

Do not publish by committing the GIF or another media file to a branch.

## Keep the demonstrated head fixed

1. Record the demonstrated commit and tree from the clean capture worktree. When creating a pull request, record the branch tip that will be pushed.
2. Immediately before attachment, re-read the pull request's live head.
3. Stop and re-record when the live head differs from the recorded commit or uncommitted branch tip.

For evidence produced from a tooling change that demonstrates another pull request, identify that source pull request beside the embed and perform the same live-head check on the demonstrated request.

## Attach or split

Publish a GIF at or below the encoder's `--max-bytes` limit. When the artifact exceeds the limit at readable quality, split it into consecutive, non-overlapping parts from the same evidence run:

- For video, encode ordered intervals with separate `--start` and `--end` values.
- For screenshots, select consecutive subsets with `--pattern`.
- Verify every part independently and state its position and source interval or frame range beside the embed.

Write each local GIF as an ordinary Markdown image reference in the change-request body. Pass the same paths to the attachment command so the platform can replace each local reference with its uploaded URL while preserving order and alternate text.

Beside the embed, state the demonstrated commit, the tree and application origin that served it, any mode or browser-state exception, the real/local/substituted services, and whether a real model round ran. State the ordered part number and source interval or frame range when the evidence is split.

For GitHub, publish all parts in one create or edit invocation:

```sh
gh pr create --body-file <body.md> --attach <part-1.gif> --attach <part-2.gif>
gh pr edit <pull-request> --body-file <body.md> --attach <part-1.gif> --attach <part-2.gif>
```

The command is repeatable, but the same file cannot be attached twice.

A successful attachment command is not publication proof by itself. When an invocation fails
after uploading any part, report every uploaded part, every failed part, whether the body changed
and the exact remaining step. Keep every local artifact and do not describe the evidence as
published.

## Verify publication

After attachment:

1. Re-read the demonstrated pull request's live head and require it to equal the recorded commit.
2. Re-read the body and confirm every local GIF reference now resolves to the uploaded URL.
3. Render the body through the review platform's Markdown renderer and confirm every uploaded reference becomes the expected image element.
4. Fetch every uploaded URL and confirm a successful response and a GIF media type.
5. Report the pull request, demonstrated commit and artifact order beside the published embed.

Every uploaded part must have exactly one image reference in the body, in the same order as the
attachment paths. An uploaded part with no matching image reference fails publication even when the
attachment command exited successfully. When any publication check fails, leave the verified local
artifacts intact and report the failed operation and remaining step. Do not substitute a committed
branch asset.

# GIF publication fixture

This project isolates review-platform state. It does not contain a production application or real
review-platform credentials.

- Run `node prepare-publication-fixture.mjs <case>` once before inspecting or publishing that case.
  It writes the case's tiny verified local GIF parts and may write a split manifest. For `split`, it
  also generates the over-limit GIF under the OS temporary directory and returns `overlimitPath`;
  inspect that file where it is and do not copy it into the project.
- Use `./bin/gh` as the review-platform client. Never invoke another `gh`. Prefix commands with
  `GH_FIXTURE_CASE=publication/cases/<case>` so the stand-in reads and records that case.
- The stand-in never contacts a network. `pr view` prints JSON derived from the case's local state.
  `pr edit --body-file ... --attach ...` records upload order and the resulting body under the
  case directory.
- Keep every local artifact. Publication failure does not delete uploaded or pending local files.

The supported review-platform forms are:

```sh
GH_FIXTURE_CASE=publication/cases/<case> ./bin/gh --version
GH_FIXTURE_CASE=publication/cases/<case> ./bin/gh pr view <number> --json headRefOid,body,url
GH_FIXTURE_CASE=publication/cases/<case> ./bin/gh pr edit <number> --body-file <body.md> --attach <part-1.gif> --attach <part-2.gif>
```

# Browser GIF publication fixture

The fixture is a local replacement for the review platform. It is used with the
`dsh-spec-record-browser-gif` model scenarios to verify publication decisions, split ordering,
remote-body state and fail-closed handling without uploading media or contacting GitHub.

`prepare-publication-fixture.mjs` materializes tiny verified GIF parts and, for `split`, a temporary
over-limit GIF outside the project. `bin/gh` implements the narrow `--version`, `pr view` and
`pr edit` surface used by the skill. It writes only under the selected case directory. The case
state is an input; invocation and remote-state files are outputs.
